title: Generation, culture, and stimulation of small intestinal murine organoids in parasitology research
protocol: Dissect the most proximal 10 cm of the small intestine.
Flush the dissected tissue with 5 mL ice-cold PBS using a syringe and a pipette tip.
Cut the tissue longitudinally and wash out remaining intestinal contents.
Gently scrape the upper mucosa with a coverslip.
Transfer the scraped tissue to a Falcon tube with 15 mL ice-cold PBS.
Transport the Falcon tube back to the laboratory on ice.
In the laboratory, transfer the Falcon tube contents onto a Petri dish.
Cut gut tissue into small pieces (1–2 mm) using scissors.
Transfer the cut tissue to a fresh Falcon tube with a serological pipette and make up to 10 mL total volume with ice-cold PBS.
Gently pipette up/down with a serological pipette ×10.
Allow the mixture to settle, remove PBS, and repeat wash with 10 mL ice-cold PBS twice more.
Aspirate the PBS and add 20 mL of 2 mM EDTA in ice-cold PBS.
Incubate for 30 minutes at 4°C on a roller.
Remove PBS-EDTA solution after incubation.
Add 10 mL ice-cold PBS, mix gently ×10.
Allow tissue fragments to settle and collect supernatant in a tube (Fraction 1).
Repeat the process with more vigorous pipetting each time until six fractions are collected.
Transfer 20 μL from each fraction into a 96-well plate.
Observe the crypt concentration under a 4× objective in an inverted microscope.
Combine crypt-enriched fractions into a 50 mL Falcon tube through a 70 μm cell strainer.
Wash the cell strainer with 5 mL ice-cold PBS and spin at 300 g for 3 min at 4°C to pellet crypts.
Spin crypts again at 400 g if they fail to pellet initially.
Thaw MG on ice to prevent solidifying.
Alternatively, thaw MG at 4°C before starting and keep on ice to prevent solidifying.
Remove supernatant from the sample and add 10 mL ADF Base.
Move the sample to a 15 mL Falcon for easier pelleting.
Spin the sample at 100 g for 3 min at 4°C and remove the supernatant.
Add another 10 mL of ADF Base after removing supernatant.
Take 20 μL and count crypts as in step i.
Spin the amount to be plated in a 15 mL Falcon at 300 g for 3 min at 4°C; aim to plate 500 crypts/well/50 μL MG in a 24-well plate.
Remove supernatant and gently resuspend the pellet in MG (500 μL is enough for ∼12 wells).
Plate out on a pre-warmed at 37°C well plate - 50 μL/well.
Work swiftly to avoid solidification and bubbles when mixing MG with crypts.
Incubate for 10 minutes at 37°C to allow MG to solidify.
Add 500 μL/well of ADF Org + all growth factors (EGF, R-spondin, Noggin, ChiR) to the side of the well to prevent disrupting the MG dome containing crypts.
Change the media on day 2 without disrupting the MG.
Wash Falcon tubes, tips, and serological pipettes briefly in ADF Base to prevent tissue from sticking to plastics.
Passage organoids every 4/5 days starting two days after the first media change.
Add 500 μL/well of ADF Org + growth factors (EGF, R-spondin, Noggin) and incubate at 37°C.
Aspirate media from organoids and add 1 mL ice-cold ADF Base.
Break up Matrigel (MG) with a 10 mL serological pipette, scraping gently.
Combine up to 10 samples into a 15 mL Falcon tube, making up to 10 mL with ice-cold ADF Base if needed, and spin at 300 g for 3 min at 4°C.
Aspirate media from the pellet and add 1 mL ice cold ADF base.
Gently break up MG with a 1 mL pipette.
Add 10 mL ADF Base and spin at 300 g for 3 min at 4°C.
Repeat steps of aspirating, adding ADF Base, breaking up MG, and spinning until all MG is removed.
Aspirate media from the pellet and use a P200 to disrupt the pellet and break the organoids gently twice.
Add 10 mL ADF Base and spin at 100 g for 3 min.
Aspirate media and add 10 mL ADF Base.
Take 20 μL of the mixture and count the number of crypts.
Spin the amount to be plated in a 15 mL Falcon tube at 300 g for 3 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and add 500 μL MG.
Plate out 50 μL per well using a Nunc Lab-Tek II Chamber Slide System for induction experiments, use 30 μL MG per well.
Incubate for 10 minutes at 37°C to allow MG to solidify.
Add crypt media (ADF Org + growth factors EGF, Noggin, and R-Spondin).
Change the media every 2 days without disrupting the MG.
Aspirate media and add 1 mL ice cold ADF Base per well for freezing organoids.
Break up the Matrigel (MG) with a P1000 tip gently.
Combine the broken-up MG into a 15 mL Falcon tube (3 wells of organoids/15 mL).
Spin at 150 g for 10 min at 4°C and aspirate media.
Repeat steps until all MG is removed.
Resuspend in 1 mL Gibco Cell Recovery freezing media.
Transfer 1 mL to cryovials and freeze at -80°C, then store in LN2 the following day.
Thaw rapidly at 37°C in a water bath.
Spin at 300 g for 3 min at 4°C and aspirate media.
Add 1 mL of ADF, transfer to a 15 mL Falcon tube and make up the volume to 10 mL with ice-cold ADF.
Spin at 300 g for 3 min at 4°C and aspirate media.
Add 500 μL MG (enough for ∼12 wells).
Plate out 50 μL/well.
Incubate for 10 min at 37°C to allow MG to solidify.
Incubate at 37°C with crypt media (ADF Org + growth factors: EGF, Noggin, R-Spondin, and ChiR initially).
Change the media every 2 days without disrupting the MG.
Add 500 μL/well of ADF Org + growth factors (EGF, Noggin, and R-Spondin).
Split organoids at least four times before experimental treatments.
Plate fresh organoids in low concentration (200 crypts/well in 30 μL MG) into Nunc Lab-Tek II Chamber Slide System - 8-well chamber slide.
Add 200 μL ADF Org + growth factors to each well and incubate at 37°C.
Remove media without disrupting the MG on Day 2.
Add 200 μL/well of ADF Org + growth factors to each well and incubate at 37°C.
Remove media without disrupting the MG on Day 3.
Add 200 μl/well of ADF Org + growth factors + stimulants to each well and incubate at 37°C.
Take pictures of organoids with an inverted microscope or EVOS imaging system using 4×, 10× and/or 20× objectives.
Take pictures of organoids with an inverted microscope or EVOS imaging system using 4×, 10× and/or 20× objectives.
Harvest the cultures for assays as needed.
Analyze morphological changes by bright field microscopy.
Disperse single cells for flow cytometry analysis.
Stain intact or sectioned organoids for immunofluorescence analysis.
Extract RNA from organoids for qPCR or RNA sequencing.
Replace media with 1 mL cold ADF base and scrape organoids off the plate into the media using a 10 mL serological pipette.
Transfer the detached organoids in MG/media to a 15 mL falcon tube, top up to 10 mL with cold ADF base.
Spin at 300 g for 4 minutes.
Aspirate off the media and use a P200 to gently disrupt the pellet ten times.
Add 0.5-1 mL TrypLE express and 2000 units/mL DNase II to detached organoids.
Leave samples at 37°C for 20–25 minutes to dissociate organoids.
Place samples in a 37°C incubator shaker to encourage dissociation.
Inactivate TrypLE by adding 5 mL of ADF base with 5% FCS after incubation.
Pipette the supernatant 5–10 times to further dissociate organoids.
Pass the cell suspension through a 40 μm cell strainer.
Count cells using trypan blue.
Calculate the number of cells and plate them appropriately for flow analysis.
Resuspend the correct amount of cells in PBS after spinning down at 400 g for 5 minutes.
Plate cells into a 96-well round-bottomed plate.
Spin down samples at 400 g for 5 minutes at 4°C and wash once more with PBS (100 μL per well).
Incubate with live/dead dye (BV506, 1:1000 dilution) for 30 minutes at 4°C in the dark.
Wash samples with 200 μL of PBS after spinning down at 400 g for 5 minutes.
Block using rat IgG (1:50) for 20 minutes at 4°C.
Wash samples using FACS buffer (add to the well, then spin at 400 g for 5 minutes).
Stain cells in 50 μL of extracellular stain mix diluted at a 1:200 ratio in FACS buffer or Brilliant Stain Buffer if using two or more BD Brilliant dyes.
Incubate the stained cells for 35 min at 4°C in the dark.
Wash by adding 150 μL PBS, then centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min.
Resuspend the washed cells in 50 μL PBS and fix with 100 μL of 4% PFA.
Incubate the fixed cells at room temperature for 15 min.
Wash once with 200 μL PBS, then centrifuge to collect cells.
Permeabilize cells by treating them in 150 μL PBS containing 1% Triton X-100 for 15 min at room temperature.
Stain the permeabilized cells with 50 μL of intracellular antibodies suspended in PBS and 1% BSA, incubating them in the dark at room temperature for 1 h.
If using secondary antibodies for intracellular staining, wash once more with 150 μL perm buffer.
Incubate stained cells in 50 μL secondary antibodies if needed, leaving them in the dark for 30 min at room temperature.
Wash twice with 200 μL FACS buffer to prepare the samples for analysis.
Analyze the cell suspension using a flow cytometer or use a cell sorter to isolate specific cell populations for further biological assays.
Aspirate the medium from each well of intestinal organoids.
Wash the wells twice in cold PBS.
Fix the cells with 4% paraformaldehyde, incubating them at room temperature for 20 min.
Rinse wells once in PBS and store in 500 μL/well PBS.
Wrap wells with parafilm to avoid drying out.
Permeabilize with PBS containing 0.5% Triton X-100 for 10 min at 4°C.
Rinse 3 times with PBS/Glycine (1× PBS; 100 mM glycine), 10–15 min per wash at room temperature.
Incubate with 200 μL/well IF buffer for 45–60 min at room temperature.
Incubate with the primary antibody in Antibody Dilution Buffer overnight (15–18 h) at room temperature.
Rinse 3 times (5–10 min each) with IF Buffer at room temperature with gentle rocking.
Incubate with fluorescent conjugated secondary antibody in Antibody Dilution Buffer for 40–50 min at room temperature.
Rinse once (5 min) with IF Buffer at room temperature with gentle rocking.
Rinse 2–3 times with PBS (5 min) at room temperature.
Remove chambers from slides.
Add nuclear stain (DAPI 1:10,000 in water for 10 min).
Rinse 2–3 times with PBS (5 min) at room temperature.
Mount with VECTASHIELD.
Aspirate medium from each well.
Wash wells with 400 μL ice-cold PBS.
Add 400 μL Trizol to each well, in the fume hood.
Incubate on ice for 10 min, to help MG dissolve.
Pipette up and down to completely dissolve MG and transfer to an Eppendorf tube.
Vortex for 10 s.
Store the leptin-CRP solution at −80°C until ready to continue with RNA extraction.
Centrifuge the supernatant at 12,000 g for 2 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a new Eppendorf tube to remove debris.
Add 100 μL chloroform to the supernatant and mix well.
Incubate at room temperature for 3 min.
Centrifuge at 12,000 g for 15 min at 4°C.
Transfer the upper aqueous phase to a new Eppendorf tube.
Add 1.5 volumes of 100% ethanol to precipitate RNA.
Mix well by inverting the tube several times.
Proceed to RNA purification using RNeasy Mini kit following manufacturer’s instructions.
